slides.visual_cue:
Slide 1
Title Slide
slides.narration: Welcome to the Spoken Tutorial on Creating a Database using pgAdmin4.

slides.visual_cue:
Slide 2
Learning Objectives
slides.narration:
In this tutorial we will learn to,
Connect the database to the server, and
Create a database.

slides.visual_cue:
Slide 3
System Requirements
slides.narration:
To record this tutorial, I am using 
Ubuntu Linux OS v24.04 
PostgreSQL version 18.1 and 
pgAdmin4 version 9.11

slides.visual_cue:
Slide 4
Pre-requisites 

https://EduPyramids.org
slides.narration:
To follow this tutorial, 
Learners should have installed PostgreSQL and pgAdmin4.
For the pre-requisite, PostgreSQL tutorials, please visit this website.
Let us open the pgAdmin4.

slides.visual_cue:
Go to Show Apps and search for pgAdmin4, click on the icon.

Cursor on the interface.
slides.narration:
Go to Show Apps and search for pgAdmin4, click on the icon.

pgAdmin 4 interface is open now.

slides.visual_cue:
Cursor on Object.


Zoom in  (Press Ctrl ++)to see the objects clearly while recording.


Click on the Properties tab, and show the cursor on the tab.
slides.narration:
On the left hand side we can see the object browser pane.
The various objects of the database  will be displayed here.
In the toolbar, the Properties tab shows the relevant properties of each object.

slides.visual_cue:
Click on the SQL tab, and show the cursor on the tab.


Point to the text shown brown colour.
slides.narration:
Besides Properties, we have a SQL tab.

The tab displays the script of the selected object.
As of now no SQL query is shown.
Let us now see how to connect to the server.

slides.visual_cue:
Go to the left panel, right click on Servers.

Select Register and then select Servers.


Cursor on Register -Server window.
slides.narration:
In the left panel, right click on Servers.
A context menu opens. 

Select Register and then select Servers.

Register -Server window displays.

slides.visual_cue:
Under General, in the name tab type localhost.

Click on the Connection tab.
In the Host name/address type: localhost.
slides.narration:
Under General, in the Name field type: localhost.

Click on the Connection tab.
In the Host name/address type: localhost.

slides.visual_cue: Leave the other parameters as default.
slides.narration: Let us keep all the other parameters as default.

slides.visual_cue:
Point the cursor on the Maintenance database name and Username.

Enter password as: postgres
Click on Save button.
slides.narration:
Note that, Maintenance database name and Username fields are already filled. 
Please enter the password which is given during installation.
Click on Save button at the bottom right corner.

Localhost Dashboard opens.

slides.visual_cue:
In the left panel, point the cursor to the localhost.

Click on the localhost node drop down arrow.

Point the cursor to the objects.
slides.narration:
Here, we can see that a connection is  established to the localhost. 

Click on the localhost node.
We can see the following objects for this particular server.

slides.visual_cue:
Now click on the Databases node drop down arrow.

Point the cursor to the default postgres database
slides.narration:
Now click on the Databases node. 

The default database postgres created during installation is displayed here.

slides.visual_cue:
Slide 5

What is Database?
slides.narration:
A database is a collection of information or data, which is stored in an organized way.
A Database has objects such as tables, views, procedures, functions and others.

slides.visual_cue:
Go back to pgAdmin.


Right click on Databases node select Create, from the sub menu select Database.

Cursor on Create-Databases window.
slides.narration:
Now, we will create a new database.

Right click on Databases node select Create, from the sub menu select Database.

Create-Databases window displays.

slides.visual_cue:
Type database name: Studentdb and click Save.


Cursor on the Studentdb database.
slides.narration:
Type Studentdb as the database name and click Save.

Now the newly created database is listed under the Database node.

slides.visual_cue:
Click on the X button to close the window.


Point to the pop window. 
Point to the message.

Click the blue Yes button to close the window.
slides.narration:
Click on the close button to close the window.

A pop window Quit PgAdmin 4 opens.
It shows a message Are you sure you want to quit the application?

Click the blue Yes button to close the window.

Summary
